lens: L3 blast radius of one run. One run replaces the whole worklist (Detector.save: DELETE FROM findings, then every item recomputed) and nothing bounds how much it changes before people and payers see it. The snapshot has no swing check at all, and the self-check that should catch a vanishing is not wired into either cycle (no caller in the snapshot or the dev tree f9a326e). Even once wired, on invented data both the snapshot's and the dev tree's self-check let through, with every check green: a 1,600-item flood, 800 items leaving Work now by state, a cut-short copy dropping 30 items (excused as 'superseded'), 500 closures with proof ($50,000 counted as recovered), 300 let-gos by a hide rule, 300 relabels, a $150,000 re-pricing. And a held run still faxes payers, clears alerts and mails the weekly report. Normal real runs are small (per remittance day p99 70 new items and 50 closures; per 100 remittance lines p99 7.31 and 4.73, max 13.76 and 4.85), so a guard can hold every case above with no false holds on the 145 weeks on record. Observed on the real Vercel image: one release run reopened 550 items ($27,017) and took 1,549 off the list with no person in between. Tests: guard/L3/test_l3_blast_radius.py (23 fail, 4 controls pass); measurements: guard/L3/measure/*.json.

class_guard:
SWING GUARD SPEC (one module, remitwatch/swing.py; one call in Detector.save; both hosts).
1. Where. Detector.save builds the candidate (out_rows, with hide rules, folds, states, expected values and any archive retirement applied to it in memory) and calls swing.assess(conn, published, candidate, ctx) BEFORE `DELETE FROM findings`. Only a passing or released candidate is written; the serving copy (Vercel) and every page read only the published list. The self-check's after_detection runs on what was written.
2. Transitions. Per item, published vs candidate: appear (new listed id), vanish (listed id gone or stale), enter, leave (listed to not listed, item still on record: Done, Expired, Can't check, Accepted, Let go), close, reopen, relabel (same line or claim, new id), money (shortfall or expected value change of $1 or more), deadline (moved over 7 days). Kept per run as a transition record (item, from, to, money before and after, cause) plus a rollup by category, signal, payer group, status and work_state (replaces progress_snapshots as what alarms read).
3. Causes (first match wins). person: a person's event on the item since the last published run (status, a hide rule a person made, the owner's policy decision). facts: the item's own-claim fingerprint changed (selfcheck._facts_of extended with supersession of its remittance, its EMA lines, newest postings and newest A/R row). calendar: a date the item carries (appeal or legal deadline, follow-up day, NO_ANSWER due day) falls between the last published run's day and today. release: DETECT_VERSION changed, a migration ran, or this is the first EMA report of its kind. shared: anything else (one store-, payer- or period-wide value moved: L1's class).
4. Thresholds (constants with the measurement that set them; real archive 2024-01 to 2026-10, aggregates in guard/L3/measure). Cumulative from the last published state and per calendar day, over all runs and hops.
 - facts: appear+enter <= 20 + 15 per 100 new remittance lines read (max week on record 13.76 per 100, 439 items); close <= 20 + 6 per 100 lines (max 4.85, 178); reopen <= 20 unless the item's own claim shows a reversal; EMA-driven moves per EMA file: budget measured on the B world before release (owner INT).
 - shared: 20 items, $5,000, and 10 items in any one payer group (normal value 0 by construction).
 - per payer group, any non-person cause: max(25, 3 x that group's own daily p99 for the move; e.g. Medicare KY new 48, Humana MA closed 28).
 - calendar: 20 + 3 x what the previous run predicted for the days elapsed; a 'today' that moved backwards or by more than 2 days makes calendar moves over 20 a hold.
 - money: unexplained money moves over $5,000 in total or 2% of open dollars.
 - hide rules: a rule that lets go more than max(25, what it let go when made) in one run; folds: a new pattern or more than 25 items.
 - release causes are never held for size: they publish with a notice.
 By construction no week of the 145 on record would be held; acceptance: replay the archive day by day on a copy with the guard in measure-only mode (zero holds on the 988 remittance days) and the chaos perturbations (all held).
5. What a hold does. Published list kept; candidate stored compressed (selfcheck_held's store) with its run id and transition record. Admitted from the candidate while held: every person's change (already published) and 'facts' appears within the cumulative budget (new work still shows). Held: closures, reopenings, leaves, vanishes, relabels, money moves, unexplained appears, hide and fold let-gos over their budgets, archive retirement, expected-value rewrite. Frozen outward and permanent effects: automatic faxes (follow-ups, retries) and bulk appeal; alert clears (the engine may add, never clear); the weekly report's new-work list (it says the update was held); Results freezes and the baseline.
6. What people see. Every page, above everything, on both hosts (from meta, so Vercel's copy shows it): 'RemitWatch held today's update. It would have added N items ($X), closed M ($Y) and moved K off the list. Most have nothing new on their own claim (one shared value moved). The list is yesterday's, with your changes. See what changed.' The Data tab lists the transitions by cause, signal and payer group with example finding ids (deep links), and the files read since the last published run (counts by kind, never names). A SWING alert (high) is mailed once per hold and again only if the held change grows. The diagnostic bundle carries the rollup.
7. Who releases. The owner (require_owner, as the Providers tab, typed count like H7), naming the run id shown (a newer candidate makes the release 409 changed); on Vercel a journal entry 'swing_release' {run_id, counts} applied at the next run start. Automatic release only when a later run, compared with the published list, is within every budget ('the next run agreed with the list you work'). A held vanish, leave or close wave is never auto-published by time. After 2 days held the banner turns red and the alert repeats daily. Discard: the owner names the input to take back (L2/L5) and the next run recomputes without it. Every hold, release and discard goes to the decision log with who, when and the run id.
8. Release notice (not a hold): rules version change, migration, first A/R or Production report: published with the diff and one owner acceptance; until accepted, automatic faxes for items it moved wait (7 days at most) and vanished items stay kept.
9. Also: fax.followups/api._send_followup hold any item that a non-person cause closed, reopened or moved in the last run until a person opens it; the vanished check's 'superseded' route only when the item's claim is on a current remittance; apply_hide_rules runs on the candidate and sets work_state; /api/meta serves the banner; progress_snapshots gains work_state and signal or is replaced by the transition rollup.
property_test:
Generated swing test (release gate 9; both hosts: the file store through pipeline.run_cycle and the compact store image through cloud.run_cloud_cycle with LocalState; invented data from tests/test_features, tests/test_selfcheck and tests/ema_fixtures builders).
World(seed): 3 to 8 payer groups paying weekly or twice a week, 20 to 60 weeks of 835s, optional weekly EMA exports, A/R and Production, people's statuses and faxes on 5% of items. Run the cycle to a published state P0 and record T0 (items, states, money, causes).
Perturb with exactly one of: (a) shared-value floods: one 835 from one group (adjustment-only or 1 to 3 claims) dated today-3, today+1, today+400 or 2099-12-31; a posted-scope two-day Production export; a payer alias setting change. (b) vanishings: a cut-short copy or a same-trace copy with other claims; a filtered A/R; the clock moved 15 days with no new files; a rule monkeypatched to return nothing; a hide rule matching a relabelled signal. (c) a closure wave: a Production export carrying another tenant's link prefix or duplicated postings. (d) a money swing: one E/M line 10x its allowed amount. (e) normal: the next 1 to 7 days of 835s drawn from the same model, plus people's actions, plus a calendar day passing. (f) a rules-version change and a first A/R report.
Invariants, each on both hosts:
I1 for (a) to (d) whose transitions pass a threshold: the published list after the run (server findings, Vercel serving copy) equals P0 plus people's changes plus admitted facts-appears; meta swing:state.held is true; /api/meta carries the banner on both hosts.
I2 for (e): never held, published = candidate (no false hold on any generated normal day; also 0 holds when replaying the real archive week by week on a copy).
I3 while held: the fake fax line records zero automatic sends; notify sends exactly one SWING alert and no alert row goes to cleared; results_snapshots gets no final=1 row and no baseline is written; archive retires nothing.
I4 release is exact: after the owner releases run R, published = candidate(R) plus people's changes since; a release naming an older run id is refused.
I5 no creep: a flood split into k >= 2 runs, each under the per-run budget, is held once the cumulative change since P0 passes it (also across Vercel hops in one day).
I6 (f) publishes with swing:state.notice listing counts by signal and cause, never held for size; automatic faxes for items it moved wait until accepted.
I7 the verdict (held, counts by move and cause) is identical on the file store and the compact image.
I8 a second cycle with no new input changes nothing: same verdict, no second SWING mail, no item moves.
I9 attribution is sound: every transition the run records has exactly one cause; removing the perturbation input (L2 take-back) and running again returns the published list to P0 plus admitted changes.
